east_texas.headline: Sunny and dry. Chilly start, mild afternoon.
east_texas.summary: Many areas saw their first frost of the season this morning, and a few of the coldest spots dropped below freezing for the first time. The afternoon turns sunny and mild, in the mid 60s, with a light east wind. Another clear night, a little milder than last night.

days.text: Mild and dry, a bit more humid.
Weak front. A stray sprinkle at most, slightly cooler.
Pattern change. Better odds of widespread rain and cooler air for Thanksgiving week.

facts.p: No notable outages in East Texas

panels.title: Wetter and cooler, but no Arctic air
paras: NWS Shreveport and Fort Worth both point to a pattern change early next week. A slow storm system over the Gulf Coast could bring a soaking rain Mon–Tue, then cooler days through the holiday. The Climate Prediction Center favors above-normal rain for Texas Nov 22–26.
Freezing nights look unlikely through the end of November.

panels.title: A strong El Niño is in charge
paras: El Niño is now strong and still strengthening, near +2.5°C in the key Pacific region. That usually means an active southern storm track, with more rain and more cool, cloudy days in East Texas.
It does not bring Arctic air on its own. Ice or snow still needs cold air from Canada, and Canada is running warm right now.

east_texas.sources: NWS Shreveport forecast and discussion, NWS Fort Worth, Storm Prediction Center, NOAA Climate Prediction Center, KLTV closings, PowerOutage.us.

nm.headline: Snow showers tonight, then a very cold Wednesday night.
nm.summary: A weak storm brings rain and snow showers this evening into early Wednesday. NWS Albuquerque expects several inches above 9,000 ft in the northern Sangres and Tusas, with mostly rain in the valleys. Skies clear Wednesday, and the high valleys turn very cold that night.

days.text: Rain and snow showers. Several inches possible on peaks above 9,000 ft. Gusty southwest wind.
Sunny and cooler. Clear, calm and very cold at night in the high valleys.
Windy Friday. Some mountain snow Friday night into Saturday, mainly the Tusas.
A quick storm with wider rain and mountain snow. Models agree it is coming. Amounts are still uncertain.

nm.snow_note: Last weekend's snow is still holding on north-facing high terrain. Most south and east slopes below 9,500 ft are patchy or bare.
nm.ski_note: Sipapu is making snow and reports a 5 in. base, which includes man-made snow. Dates with ~ are projected and may change.

panels.title: Angel Fire could hit 10° Wednesday night
paras: Fresh snow, clear skies and calm wind let cold air pool in high basins like the Moreno Valley. Angel Fire is forecast near 10°F, and other sheltered valleys can run well below forecast too. Protect outdoor pipes and pets.

panels.title: Mountain routes clear for now
paras: NMRoads shows no closures or difficult conditions on NM-518, US-64, NM-434, NM-75, NM-38 or I-25 near Las Vegas as of this morning. Watch for slick spots on the passes early Wednesday.
No critical fire weather is expected for at least 7 days.

panels.title: Strong El Niño favors a snowier season
paras: El Niño is strong and still strengthening. It usually sends more storms across the southern Rockies, which improves the odds for snowfall in the northern New Mexico mountains. It doesn't guarantee a big season, but the odds lean our way.

nm.sources: NWS Albuquerque forecast and discussion, NRCS SNOTEL, NMRoads, Sipapu snow report, OnTheSnow projected openings, NOAA Climate Prediction Center.
